_sources.discrepancies: NCSL lists OK as 'photo ID requested' (non-strict). SoS confirms voters without photo ID may execute a personal affidavit and vote a regular ballot. Consistent. 2026-06-10 verification: the verification tracker suggested the 2026 primary might be June 30; the Oklahoma State Election Board confirms the primary is JUNE 16, 2026 with the runoff primary August 25, 2026. Registration deadlines corrected to the statutory 25-day rule per the State Election Board (primary: May 22, 2026 — file previously had May 15; runoff: July 31, 2026 — previously July 24). General-election early voting includes the preceding Wednesday (Oct 28-31, 2026); primaries/runoffs are Thursday-Saturday. State Election Board also confirms no recognized party has opened its 2026-2027 primaries to independents.

earlyVoting.notes: Early voting Thursday and Friday 8 a.m.-6 p.m. and Saturday 8 a.m.-2 p.m. before Election Day at your county's designated early voting location.
Early voting for the runoff: Thursday and Friday 8 a.m.-6 p.m. and Saturday 8 a.m.-2 p.m. before Election Day. If you voted in one party's primary, you may only vote in that party's runoff.
Early voting for the general election runs Wednesday through Friday 8 a.m.-6 p.m. and Saturday 8 a.m.-2 p.m. (October 28-31, 2026).
Early voting for the November general election is available Wednesday through Saturday before Election Day (October 28-31, 2026) at your county's designated early voting location.

acceptedIds: Oklahoma driver's license or ID card
Oklahoma voter identification card (free, issued by your county election board; no photo required)
votingRules.expirationRule: Photo ID must not be expired. The free voter identification card issued by your county election board is also acceptable (it has no photo and does not expire).
votingRules.impedimentDeclaration: Voters without acceptable photo ID may sign an affidavit and cast a regular (non-provisional) ballot.
votingRules.phonesAtPollsDetail: Oklahoma prohibits use of mobile phones and electronic devices in the voting booth.
additionalRules: Semi-closed primary: registered Republicans and Democrats may only vote in their own party's primary. Independents (no party) may vote in either party's primary but not both.
Runoff rule: if no candidate receives a majority in the primary, the top two advance to a runoff. A voter who voted in one party's primary may only vote in that party's runoff.

eligibility: Will be absent from the county on Election Day and early voting period
voteByMail.applicationDeadline: Must be received by the county election board 7 days before the election
voteByMail.returnDeadline: Must be received by the county election board by 7 p.m. on Election Day
voteByMail.returnDeadlinePlain: Absentee ballot must arrive at the county election board by 7 p.m. on Election Day. Postmarks do not count.

runoffRules.ruleExplanation: Oklahoma rule: if you voted in one party's primary, you can only vote in that same party's runoff. If you did not vote in the primary, you may choose either party's runoff.

primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEn: Oklahoma has a closed primary effective for 2026 (Okla. Stat. Title 26, §26-1-104). Only voters registered with a political party may vote in that party's primary. Both the Republican and Democratic parties are running closed primaries for the 2026 cycle. If a runoff occurs, party-lock rules apply.
primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEs: Oklahoma tiene una primaria cerrada vigente para 2026 (Okla. Stat. Title 26, §26-1-104). Solo los votantes registrados en un partido político pueden votar en la primaria de ese partido. Tanto el Partido Republicano como el Demócrata están realizando primarias cerradas para el ciclo 2026. Si hay una segunda vuelta, se aplican las reglas de bloqueo de partido.
